doc.title: Young Snooky — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Louie Bellson's death and plans for the funeral
summary: Young and Brown talk about Louie Bellson's recent death, the funeral arrangements, and Brown's earlier interview with him.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Louie Bellson? Young:…Louie Bellson. We just lost him, we just losing so many good people now, man. Louie Bellson, Thursday. Are you going to be in town Thursday?
We‘re leaving Thursday morning.
You‘re leaving Thursday morning.
Yeah, but we hope to catch it, because I leave in San Francisco. So they‘re going to do a service for him in San Jose.
Oh, they are?
Yeah, because that‘s where he lived. His last house was in San Jose, so I want to go to the service there.
Well, I‘m going to try and make his funeral here…
Thursday.
Thursday.
Right, five o‘clock, I think.
Yeah, five o‘clock. Four o‘clock showing…

Right. Young:…five o‘clock, you know. So I‘m going if I can get somebody to go with me, I can‘t go by myself. I‘m going to try and get somebody to go with me, that‘s why I mentioned it to you, were you going to be in town.
If we would be here we would go together. [laughs]
I know we would, I know we would. That‘s too bad that you‘re not, and he‘s a drummer just like you.
We did the interview with him also.
You did what?
We interviewed him as well, the same way we‘re doing you…
You did? Brown:…we did, yeah, about five, four years ago.
Oh yeah, he‘s a great cat, man. Beautiful person…
Beautiful, yeah, big heart, big heart. All heart.
